paths.description: Public landing and content archetype: audited purpose, navigation, responsive rendering, preferences, crawlability, performance, security, sustainability, and memory; represents the publicly reachable informational sections.
Primary sign-in journey and authentication template: audited SSO choice, narrow reflow, semantic structure, and handoff behavior up to the external identity-provider boundary.

Authenticated Noor application and identity-provider account steps were not covered because no credentials were supplied; this is outside the public-site audit boundary, not an unexecuted registered check.

findings.summary: The landing page ignores the system dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots under light and prefers-color-scheme: dark are pixel-identical; the page remains a white/light surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and derive surfaces/text from prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), while preserving the existing manual theme control.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion users still receive entrance motion and auto-advancing carousels.
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce active, the probe found two fadeInBottom animations lasting 1.75s and 2s plus two ride=carousel components.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential keyframes and auto-advance inside a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce query; retain manual carousel controls.

findings.summary: Navigation relies on abrupt ASP.NET postbacks with no transition continuity.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe shows primary navigation as javascript:__doPostBack links and no authored transition evidence; route changes replace the document abruptly.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real URLs and progressive cross-document View Transitions, with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Scroll-related presentation does not use declarative scroll timelines.
findings.evidence: The page probe found zero scroll timelines; all observed motion is conventional keyframe/carousel behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Where scroll-linked effects are retained, implement them with CSS animation-timeline rather than JavaScript scroll work.

findings.summary: Carousel and mobile navigation use legacy framework behavior rather than platform-native interaction patterns.
findings.evidence: DOM and CSS inspection found Bootstrap carousel/navigation code, no scroll timeline, and no scroll-snap or native gesture evidence on the primary surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-snap/overscroll behavior and native controls for swipeable content, preserving keyboard controls.

findings.summary: The fixed header does not adapt to scroll position.
findings.evidence: The mobile probe identifies a position-fixed header, while source inspection found no scroll-state container query or progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state query or restrained sticky-header state to reduce chrome after scrolling.

findings.summary: Postback navigation provides no focus or visual continuity cue.
findings.evidence: Primary section links are javascript postbacks, and no authored view transition/highlight cue was found in the DOM/CSS probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Move focus to the new page heading and use directional transitions or target highlighting after navigation.

findings.summary: The collapsible navigation and settings panel are custom/Bootstrap div structures rather than modern semantic disclosure primitives.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found zero dialog, popover, or details elements while the mobile UI includes a collapsible menu and a 400px settings panel.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover/details for transient disclosure with declarative light-dismiss and explicit accessible names.

findings.summary: The hero is visibly cropped on a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile screenshot shows the Arabic announcement cut off on both sides. body overflow-x:hidden masks overflow, so layout metrics report no scrollbar while content is still lost.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the hero media intrinsically responsive with max-inline-size:100%, object-fit, and an uncropped mobile source/layout; do not hide overflow to conceal loss.

findings.summary: Components rely on global breakpoints rather than container-aware adaptation.
findings.evidence: The page probe found zero container queries, while the same navigation/settings components are placed in constrained mobile containers.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type and focused @container rules for reusable cards, header, and settings UI.

findings.summary: Several interactive targets are smaller than the recommended touch area.
findings.evidence: The 360px probe measured the login button at 42.9px high, footer links at 34.7px, and social-icon links around 22-28px.
findings.suggestedFix: Give all interactive targets at least a 44px hit area, preserving visible keyboard focus and spacing adjacent targets.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is very slow in the mobile Lighthouse run.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 13.3s, FCP 3.8s, Speed Index 5.2s, and performance 0.64; the independent trace measured LCP 3.71s on an unthrottled run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, reduce redirects/render blockers, and defer non-critical scripts and below-fold media.

findings.summary: The 2.04MB load has a long render-blocking and poorly cached dependency path.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 46 requests and 2,043,486 transferred bytes, seven very-high-priority stylesheets, three parser-blocking legacy scripts, redirects, and four large advertisement/hero images without cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer scripts, remove redirect hops, preload the actual LCP asset, and set durable immutable caching on versioned media.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 117KiB unused JavaScript and 84KiB unused CSS; Font Awesome JS alone transfers 410,531 bytes in the HAR.
findings.suggestedFix: Tree-shake or replace Font Awesome, split route CSS, and load analytics/monitoring only when justified.

findings.summary: Meaningful images and links lack accessible alternatives.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found two images without alt; Lighthouse image-alt failed on footer imagery, and the link inventory contains multiple image/icon links with empty text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate alt text or empty alt for decorative images, and accessible names for icon/image links.

findings.summary: The landing page lacks a document language and has broken heading/landmark structure.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe reports empty html lang/dir and no main landmark; the H1 is empty. Lighthouse failed html-has-lang and heading-order on seven H6 elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Set html lang="ar" dir="rtl", provide one meaningful H1 and main landmark, and use sequential headings based on document structure.

findings.summary: A third-party Cloudflare script fails during page load.
findings.evidence: HAR and Lighthouse console evidence report net::ERR_SSL_VERSION_OR_CIPHER_MISMATCH for rocket-loader.min.js.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the stale loader or serve a compatible, necessary version; keep production console/network errors at zero.

findings.summary: Image delivery lacks basic sizing and responsive hygiene.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 14 of 18 images without dimensions, 13 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 15 legacy-format images, and six raster images without srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width/height, responsive srcset/sizes, lazy loading below the fold, and modern image formats.

findings.summary: Core links depend on javascript: URLs and legacy postback wiring.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe lists most navigation and login actions as javascript:__doPostBack or javascript:;, preventing normal URL semantics and graceful browser behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Render real href destinations and progressively enhance actions; retain standard open/copy/bookmark/history behavior.

findings.summary: Core internal links are not crawler-friendly and robots.txt is invalid.
findings.evidence: Most internal links are javascript postbacks. Lighthouse reports 359 robots.txt errors because /robots.txt redirects to and serves an HTML page.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid text/plain robots.txt and use real href URLs for all navigable destinations.

findings.summary: Indexing signals disagree with the public landing page.
findings.evidence: The landing canonical points to Login.aspx?ref=noor; /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml both redirect into login HTML instead of serving their formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a self-consistent canonical for the landing page and serve a valid sitemap/robots policy with successful content-type/status responses.

findings.summary: Social metadata contains malformed URLs and no structured entity data.
findings.evidence: og:url, og:image, and twitter:image use https:/ with one slash; no JSON-LD was found despite the page representing a government education organization/service.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct absolute social URLs and add JSON-LD accurately describing the organization/service and visible page content.

findings.summary: The final document lacks core security headers and sets insecure session/tracking cookies.
findings.evidence: Headers primitive found no CSP or HSTS. Cookie audit found six of seven cookies without Secure, including ASPSESSIONIDSQASRDDQ without HttpOnly, and most use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure, HttpOnly, and appropriate SameSite on session cookies; deploy HSTS and a nonce/hash-based CSP after compatibility testing.

findings.summary: Third-party analytics and monitoring dominate the transfer budget.
findings.evidence: Tracker scan found seven third-party origins including Google Analytics; HAR attributes 1,291,653 of 2,043,486 bytes to third parties and shows 400-day GA cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize and consent-gate analytics, shorten retention, self-host necessary assets, and remove monitoring code without demonstrated user value.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent on the final page.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence reports missing clickjacking protection, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy in addition to CSP/HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, nosniff, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Primary navigation and sign-in actions do not work as links without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Although raw HTML contains content, the DOM shows the core navigation and authentication controls as javascript:__doPostBack links.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve real URLs and forms first, then enhance postback/navigation behavior with JavaScript.

findings.summary: Machine-readable and missing routes are redirected into HTML rather than returning intentional failure/resource states.
findings.evidence: Direct requests for robots.txt and sitemap.xml both return 302 redirects into login/landing HTML; Lighthouse parses the HTML as 359 robots errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Return correct status codes and content types, and provide a useful 404/network recovery page rather than blanket redirects.

findings.summary: The Arabic landing page does not declare language/direction and overwhelmingly uses physical CSS.
findings.evidence: Landing html has no lang or dir. CSS inspection counted 9 logical-property occurrences versus 1,443 physical left/right declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare ar/rtl and migrate layout to logical properties so translation and bidi variants preserve reading order.

findings.summary: Media is delivered inefficiently for a mostly informational landing page.
findings.evidence: HAR transfers 661KB of images and 506KB of fonts; image inspection found 15 legacy-format files, six missing responsive sources, and three oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Use AVIF/WebP where suitable, responsive images, subset fonts, and remove duplicate logo/media downloads.

findings.summary: Non-essential analytics, monitoring, and unused framework code create avoidable work.
findings.evidence: The page loads Google Analytics, AppDynamics, Font Awesome JS and a failing Rocket Loader; Lighthouse identifies 117KiB unused JS and 84KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused libraries and defer/minimize analytics and monitoring until user value or consent requires them.

findings.summary: Third-party resources consume a disproportionate share of a simple landing page.
findings.evidence: HAR reports 13 third-party requests and 1.29MB third-party transfer, about 63% of the total; trackers include GTM/GA and AppDynamics.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt a third-party budget, self-host essential assets, and eliminate or defer third parties that do not support the core task.

taskList.title: Secure the final document and all session cookies
Repair mobile hero reflow and touch-target sizing
Reduce LCP by prioritizing the hero and removing blocking/unused payload
Restore Arabic document semantics, landmarks, headings, and accessible alternatives
Replace javascript postbacks with real URLs and progressive forms
Serve valid robots/sitemap and correct canonical/social metadata
Honor dark mode and reduced motion automatically
Modernize navigation, disclosure, and component responsiveness
Remove failing third-party loader and return intentional HTTP failure states
